clue.text: Nation first to tag bird among feathers round neck

indicators.note: among says the following pieces sit within the feathery wrap

parts.note: a boa is a feather scarf worn round the neck

indicators.note: first to picks the opening letter of the word tag

parts.note: a swan is a large water bird

explanation.surface: A nation's ornithologists ring a bird while it's draped in feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feathers round neck' is one piece, a feather boa; 'among' puts T and SWAN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Botswana is an independent country in southern Africa.

clue.text: 500 minute laps? Time must come off for motor race

indicators.note: must come off tells us a letter is removed from what has been built
laps in the sense of wraps around, so the small word encloses the numeral

parts.note: minute (my-NUTE) means very small, tiny
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Five hundred quick circuits of a track, with time cut, for a famous motor race.
explanation.walkthrough: '500' and 'laps' point at the Indianapolis 500, but 500 is the Roman D and 'laps' means wraps round.
explanation.definitionFit: Indy is the short name of the Indianapolis 500 and of IndyCar racing, an American motor race.

clue.text: Bird going after runner, hit player

indicators.note: going after puts the bird's name behind the river in the answer

parts.note: a runner in crosswords is a river; the Dee is one in Britain
a jay is a bird of the crow family

explanation.surface: A bird chases a runner and then strikes a sports player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' is crossword shorthand for a river, here the Dee.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc jockey plays the hit records, so a hit player is a radio presenter.

clue.text: Beach welcoming first of lovelies, the ultimate in Prince Harry's group

indicators.note: welcoming means the beach name takes in the next letter

parts.note: Bondi is a famous beach in Sydney

indicators.note: first of takes just the opening letter of lovelies
the ultimate in takes the final letter of Prince

explanation.surface: Prince Harry is pictured on a beach with a crowd of beautiful companions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prince Harry' reads as the royal, but Prince gives only its last letter and Harry is Debbie Harry.
explanation.definitionFit: Debbie Harry fronted the band Blondie, so it is her group.

clue.text: Paul a crackhead, Paul high — I'll put my hands up

parts.note: Paul is the setter, so he refers to himself as me

indicators.note: head of the word crack takes its first letter
high, as on drugs, signals that the letters of Paul are jumbled

explanation.surface: The setter owns up to being a high, cracked-up wreck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paul' appears twice: first as the setter (ME), then as letters scrambled by 'high' to give ULPA.
explanation.definitionFit: Mea culpa is Latin for 'my fault', an admission of guilt, like surrendering with raised arms.

clue.text: A number of owls climbing post to access the chick feeder?

indicators.note: to access means the reversed word gets inside the bird feeder

parts.note: a parent bird feeds its chicks

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: post is mail

explanation.surface: Owls clamber up a post to reach the one bringing food to the young.
explanation.definitionFit: The collective noun for a group of owls is a parliament.

clue.text: Hopeless cause, with investment of unspecified figure, is normal practice

indicators.note: investment means being clothed or enclosed, so a letter goes inside
hopeless suggests a mess, so the letters of cause are rearranged

parts.note: N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: Backing a lost cause with an undisclosed sum is how business usually goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hopeless' rearranges CAUSE into USACE; N goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Usance is an old word for custom or habitual use, and also the customary period for paying a bill.

clue.text: 3 can strip

parts.note: can and john are both slang for a toilet
to strip skin off fruit is to peel it

explanation.surface: A tin can is stripped of its label.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' points to clue 3, DEEJAY: this answer is a famous Radio 1 DJ.
explanation.definitionFit: John Peel was a celebrated BBC Radio 1 disc jockey, one of the theme's DJs.

clue.text: See 25
Witness of crimes, Pythagoras

indicators.note: of here means taken out of the following words, where the letters lie across the comma

explanation.surface: An unlikely witness to crimes: the Greek mathematician Pythagoras.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, to see, as a witness does.

clue.text: Winter weather, possibly lasting for 3

parts.note: January, abbreviated Jan, is a winter month
ice is one kind of wintry weather
long means lasting a great while

explanation.surface: Wintry weather may last for a good while.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' points to clue 3, DEEJAY: this answer is a Radio 1 DJ.
explanation.definitionFit: Janice Long was a Radio 1 presenter, the station's first woman with a daily show.

clue.text: 3 — eating nothing, it's my flab that's surprising?

indicators.note: eating means the scrambled letters take in the round letter
something surprising is unexpected, so these letters come out rearranged

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, leaving the letters of it's
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone eating nothing is amazed by their own belly.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' points to clue 3, DEEJAY. The scrambled ITS and MYFLAB give FATBYSLIM, which O goes into.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatboy Slim is the stage name of a famous DJ and producer.

clue.text: Mole yet to negotiate with Mubarak

indicators.note: to negotiate means to work things round, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spy has yet to strike a deal with the Egyptian leader Mubarak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mole' suggests a spy, fitting the Mubarak story, but it is a mark on the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole on the face, admired as an attractive blemish, is called a beauty mark.

clue.text: Allied forces primarily failing to catch terrorist leader, cursed

indicators.note: to catch means the scrambled letters close around the next letter
failing suggests going wrong, so the letters are rearranged
primarily takes the first letter of forces
leader takes the first letter of terrorist

explanation.surface: An Allied military operation fails to capture a terrorist chief and seems doomed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Failing' rearranges ALLIED plus F into ILLFAED, and T goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ill-fated is doomed or unlucky, as if under a curse.

clue.text: Wise man with two degrees taking in the Kentucky Derby, perhaps?

indicators.note: taking in means the pair of degrees encloses the next piece

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a degree; two of them are needed
MA, Master of Arts, is a degree; two of them are needed
a derby is a bowler hat, so the Kentucky one is a hat

explanation.surface: A double graduate goes to watch the famous Kentucky horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Derby' is not the race but the American name for a bowler hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma, meaning 'great soul', is a Hindu title for a revered sage, as with Gandhi.

clue.text: Topless Europeans in the distance, Italian of sorts

indicators.note: in places the shortened people inside the measure of length

parts.note: a mile is a distance

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: Danes are Europeans from Denmark

explanation.surface: Bare-chested Europeans are glimpsed far off, looking somewhat Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: A Milanese is a native of Milan, one particular kind of Italian.

clue.text: Dog that's nosy, just inquisitive, heads after bottom

indicators.note: after puts the initials behind the word for bottom

parts.note: the base is the bottom of something

indicators.note: heads takes the first letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A nosy dog sniffs the rear of others, heads following behinds.
explanation.definitionFit: The basenji is an African breed of hunting hound known for not barking.

clue.text: 3 as absorbed by happiness

indicators.note: absorbed by means the small word goes inside the word for delight

parts.note: joy is happiness
as and while can both mean during the time that

explanation.surface: A disc jockey gets lost in sheer bliss.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' points to clue 3, DEEJAY: this answer is a Radio 1 DJ.
explanation.definitionFit: Jo Whiley is a long-serving Radio 1 and Radio 2 presenter.

clue.text: Country sign bearing direction that avoids the centre

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the zodiac sign holds the next piece

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac

indicators.note: avoiding the centre means the middle letter is dropped

parts.note: south is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A road sign shows a route that bypasses the town centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a small kingdom entirely surrounded by South Africa.

clue.text: Though future perhaps healthy, given drug? Lozenge required

parts.note: past is the tense in contrast to the future, 'though' signalling the opposite
by the same contrast, ill is the opposite of healthy
E is short for ecstasy, a drug

explanation.surface: A patient hoping for good health is put on medication and needs a throat sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Though' sets up opposites: the past against the future, ill against healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastille is a small medicated sweet sucked for a sore throat, a lozenge.

clue.text: Heavyweight punching wizard right here, right now!

indicators.note: punching means the weight drives into the middle of the word for expert

parts.note: a wizard at something is an ace
a ton is a heavy weight

explanation.surface: A heavyweight boxer lands a punch on a magician, here and now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right here, right now' also nods to the theme: it is a Fatboy Slim track.
explanation.definitionFit: At once means immediately, without delay, in this very moment.

clue.text: Backing singer Jones has personal musical style

indicators.note: backing means the singer's first name is read in reverse

parts.note: Tom Jones is a Welsh singer
one's own things are personal

explanation.surface: A backing singer for Jones has a personal sound of her own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing singer' looks like a phrase, but backing is a reversal of the singer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Motown is the soul-pop sound of the Detroit record label of that name.

clue.text: Write up a novel, then fashion the subject of a comic opera

definitions.text: the subject of a comic opera

indicators.note: write up in a down clue means the title is set upwards, reversed

parts.note: Kim is a novel by Rudyard Kipling
a do, as in hairdo, is a style or fashion

explanation.surface: An author writes up a novel, then makes a comic opera of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mikado, Emperor of Japan, is the title character of Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera.

clue.text: 12 24 across, one preparing a feast fit for a conqueror?

definitions.meaning: the DJ known by the stage name at 12 and 24 across

definitions.text: one preparing a feast fit for a conqueror?
definitions.meaning: a chef catering for William the Conqueror and his people from Normandy

explanation.walkthrough: The Normans conquered England in 1066; a cook for them is cheekily a Norman cook.
explanation.definitionFit: Norman Cook is the real name of the DJ Fatboy Slim; the second sense is a Normandy chef.

clue.text: See 12
Kiss record flipped over in the middle

indicators.note: flipped in the middle means only the two central letters swap round

parts.note: a song is a record, a track

explanation.surface: A kiss is so passionate that the record spins over halfway.
explanation.definitionFit: Snog is British slang for a long passionate kiss.

clue.text: 3 carves his initial in nonsensical scrawling

indicators.note: scrawling suggests messy writing, so these letters are jumbled
initial in takes the first letter of nonsensical

explanation.surface: Someone carves his initial in a meaningless scribble.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' points to clue 3, DEEJAY: this answer is a Radio 1 DJ.
explanation.definitionFit: Chris Evans is a famous British radio presenter who hosted Radio 1's breakfast show.

clue.text: Extremes in heavy drinker, overpowering even, producing gas

indicators.note: extremes takes the first and last letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker, overpowering even, gives off gas.
explanation.walkthrough: Each of 'heavy', 'drinker', 'overpowering' and 'even' gives its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydrogen is the lightest chemical element, a colourless gas.
